source_review.notes: Reviewed PostgreSQL 18 page layout, file layout, and checksum documentation; SQLite database format and atomic-commit documentation; and MySQL 8.4 InnoDB physical-index, table-file, and disk/space-management documentation. All eight official destinations returned HTTP 200. Page size, segmentation, checksum, tablespace/file, allocation, and durability claims are scoped by engine and version.

evidence: Checked page size P, pages-per-segment N, logical block b, segment/index/offset equations, logical size, and lower/upper/special layout bounds.
Checked that database page, VM page, filesystem block/extent, device sector, relation, segment, file, and tablespace remain distinct.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Simplified equations are explicitly separated from real forks, extents, compression, encryption, and versioned engine addressing.

evidence: Recomputed block addresses around segment boundaries for blocks 0,3,4,7,8,10.
Recomputed 11 pages as segment lengths 32768,32768,24576 and total 90112 bytes.
Recomputed aligned payloads 104,200,56, lower 36, upper 7832, special 8192, and free 7796.
Recomputed additive toy checksums 12288 and 12289 after a one-byte change.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The additive checksum is deliberately weak and is labeled unusable for production integrity.

evidence: Re-derived segment and page index from Euclidean division and byte offset from fixed page size.
Re-derived segment lengths from quotient/remainder of allocated pages.
Re-derived layout validity from monotone region boundaries and alignment-inclusive payload size.
Re-derived write-ahead ordering need from data-page dependence on durable recovery log.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: No universal sector/page atomicity or flush guarantee is inferred from the mathematical model.

evidence: Reviewed block zero, last/first around segment boundaries, short files, sparse holes, maximum arithmetic, and wrong relation/fork/version identity.
Reviewed malformed headers, overlapping/out-of-range items, wrong page types, alignment, uninitialized pages, free/reusable/reclaimed distinctions, and full filesystem.
Reviewed short/torn writes, failed extension/flush, volatile caches, checksum mismatch, encryption/compression, and crash ordering.
Reviewed multi-volume snapshots, missing logs/keys, restore compatibility, immutable forensics, cancellation, and version upgrades.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Fault injection and byte-level inspection are restricted to disposable or protected copies with version-matched supported tools.

evidence: Validated each modeled offset is page aligned and within its computed segment length.
Validated segment lengths sum to logical bytes and contain exactly 11 pages.
Validated lower<=upper<=special<=page_size and free space equals upper-lower.
The verifier matched exact nine-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status.
invariant_checking.notes: The model is not a parser, checksum implementation, WAL protocol, or storage-stack simulator.

evidence: Reviewed every address tuple through divmod and offset multiplication.
Reviewed full/full/partial segment construction from 11 allocated pages.
Reviewed every layout component from header, item identifiers, alignment, payload sum, and special boundary.
Reviewed checksum change as a bounded detection example without correction/semantic claims.
proof_review.notes: No proof of a vendor format parser, storage durability, checksum collision bound, or recoverability is claimed.

evidence: Separated logical from physical addresses, file length from allocated bytes, internal free from OS-reclaimed space, and written/flushed/durable states.
Separated corruption detection from repair, matching checksum from semantic validity, and crash-consistent copy from recoverable backup.
Separated pedagogical page/segment/checksum model from PostgreSQL, SQLite, and InnoDB formats and mechanisms.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Atomic, durable, free, allocated, correct, consistent, recoverable, and verified claims require the named layer and evidence.

evidence: The standard-library finite address/layout/checksum model executed successfully through the repository verifier.
All eight final official reference destinations returned HTTP 200 on 2026-08-30.
Front matter, exact section order, local links, ten examples, five exercises, five answers, and snippet expectations passed draft validation.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No live database file, page parser, filesystem allocation, checksum tool, WAL/journal recovery, device fault, backup/restore, or performance workload was executed.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter consistently derives physical storage claims from engine/version identity, address translation, page bounds, allocation state, durability layer, and recovery evidence.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed page/file/tablespace mapping, page roles, allocation/reclamation, sparse/snapshot capacity, read/write caches, WAL/journal/torn-page mechanisms, checksums, encryption, page-size tradeoffs, backups, forensics, monitoring, faults, and upgrades.

pedagogical_review.notes: The review sheet, segment-boundary model, ten distinct systems examples, and five derivation/incident/migration exercises progress from bytes and offsets to production recovery evidence.

limitations: Internal authoring, official-source, mathematical, bounded executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and model do not certify any live database page/file format, object mapping, checksum, WAL/journal protocol, filesystem/controller/device durability, sparse allocation, backup/restore, corruption recovery, performance result, version compatibility, or production fitness.
